title: P02 follow-up: Muon decoupled weight decay 10x -> 15x (MUON_WD 0.1 -> 0.15) on the 070 incumbent, the log-midpoint between the 10x keep and the 30x break
description: P02 (Muon) follow-up on the weight-decay axis: the only edit raises the Muon group's decoupled weight decay from 10x to 15x the AdamW per-step shrinkage (MUON_WD 0.1 -> 0.15; peak per-step shrinkage 1e-3 -> 1.5e-3), leaving the AdamW group, LRs, batch, schedule, init and data identical to incumbent 070-claude. The 1x/3x/10x/30x series scored 316/327/353/(346,313,timeout), so the optimum lies between 10x and 30x or at 10x; 15x probes the lower half of that interval, where the extra plasticity/angular-rate benefit may still outweigh the slower sampling and weaker fit that broke 30x.
hypothesis: Muon adds fixed-spectral-size updates, so decoupled decay sets an equilibrium: weight norm ~sqrt(lr/wd) and per-step angular change ~sqrt(lr*wd). Raising decay 3x->10x helped (+11, +25) with unchanged val loss and higher late-round RL-solved, consistent with smaller, faster-rotating Muon weights being a more plastic start for the frozen RL AdamW (relative step ~lr_RL/||W||). At 30x (time constant ~333 steps, ~0.3 epoch memory) seeds 0/1 fell 13-22 and RL/eval sampling slowed ~100 s (longer or non-terminating samples), so too little weight mass hurt fit/termination. A parabola in log(wd) through 3x/10x/30x peaks near 10-11x with ~-3 expected at 15x; if the true peak sits above 10x (the 30x seed-2 RL-solved 879 vs 838 hints that plasticity kept rising), 15x (time constant ~667 steps, ~0.55 epoch) should gain while staying clear of the 30x failure.
expected_delta: -40 to +25 theorems at >=7 (central guess -3). Pretraining indistinguishable in speed (4700-4800 steps) with final val loss within +0.005 of 070's 0.0911/0.0913/0.0961; RL-solved at or above 070's 788/783/838 on at least two seeds if plasticity keeps rising; totals ~1080-1150 s (070: 1048/971/1079, 071 at 30x: 1147/1151/>1200), with a small (~10%) risk one seed times out in eval.

arch.change: none versus 070-claude: 5 untied fork GPT blocks, d_model 256, 8 heads (head dim 32), d_ff 1024, RoPE base 10000, LayerNorm, GELU, untied embedding/readout
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork; model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 070-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: CHANGED: MUON_WD = 15 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.15 (070-claude: 10x = 0.1), so Muon lr*0.15 is fifteen times the auxiliary AdamW lr*0.1 per-step shrinkage at every schedule fraction (peak 1.5e-3 per step instead of 1e-3; decay time constant ~667 steps at peak LR instead of ~1000). Applies to all 21 Muon matrices including head.weight. AdamW group decay (wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3) is unchanged. Summed over ~4770 steps (mean schedule factor ~0.55) the cumulative multiplicative decay factor is ~exp(-3.9)=0.02 instead of ~exp(-2.6)=0.07 (071-claude's 30x: ~exp(-7.9)).
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: standard GPT weights only; pretraining optimizer states are discarded and frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW

config.init: Exactly 070-claude: fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
